docs.title: Welcome to My Research Register
docs.text:
Welcome to my digital working notebook and technical log. This space serves as an open extension of my physical research notebooks. Here, I document literature notes, derivations, and implementation principles focused on my work in computational solid mechanics, finite element analysis, and contact mechanics.

Note: All derivations and code snippets shared here are generalized for educational purposes.

docs.title: About Me
docs.text: I am a Research Engineer in the GeM Laboratory at Nantes University, France. My current research focuses on Computational Contact Mechanics. I completed my PhD on Computational Design of Foam Based Shields for Blast Mitigation from the Department of Aerospace Engineering at IIT Bombay. Prior to my PhD, I worked as a CAE Engineer in Engine/Powertrain R&D at Maruti Suzuki India Limited. I hold a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering from NIT Srinagar.

docs.title: Research Interests
docs.text: My research interests include computational and experimental solid mechanics, with a focus on the dynamic behavior of materials and structures under extreme loading, mechanics of cellular and architectured materials, constitutive modeling, contact mechanics, topology optimization, and performance-driven material design.

docs.text: • Computational Solid Mechanics | Contact Mechanics | Dynamic Behavior of Materials | Impact and Blast Mitigation

docs.title: - Reformulating Signorini Contact Conditions via the Positive Part Operator
docs.text:
In Signorini contact mechanics, unilateral contact constraints on the boundary \(\Gamma_c\) are typically expressed through the classical complementarity conditions:

\[u_N \le g_N, \quad \sigma_N \le 0, \quad \sigma_N (u_N - g_N) = 0\]

where \(g_N\) is the normal gap function and \(\sigma_N\) is the normal contact pressure (defined negative in compression).

docs.title: - Algebraic Reformulation with the Positive Part Operator
docs.text:
To implement these non-smooth constraints efficiently in computational frameworks (such as Nitsche-based formulations in FEniCS), the complementarity system can be equivalently rewritten using the positive part operator \((\cdot)_+ = \max(0, \cdot)\).

For a given penalty parameter \(\kappa > 0\), the contact condition is compactly satisfied when:

\[\sigma_N = - \left( \kappa (u_N - g_N) - \sigma_N \right)_+\] \[\sigma_N = - \max\left( 0, \kappa (u_N - g_N) - \sigma_N \right)\]

This projection formulation maps the trial contact pressure onto the admissible region, avoiding explicit active-set search loops while ensuring thermodynamic and mechanical consistency.
